memos.headline: S02 and S08 Lead on Trend and Relative Strength; S04 and S03 Show Structural Weakness
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market across this universe today. S02 is the standout leader: +40% over 12 weeks, sitting just 0.4% off its 52-week high with RSI at 68.3 and 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +31%—this is a parabolic trend I want to ride but with tight risk management given the extended positioning (+14.3% above the 50d mean). S08 is the second-cleanest chart, only 2.5% off highs, RSI a comfortable 60.7, and strong 4-week relative strength of +6.1% vs SPY with low ATR of 1.86%. On the other side, S04 is deeply broken—down 23.1% from its 52-week high, below its 200d mean by 8.7%, and losing relative strength over both 4- and 12-week windows. S03 just printed an RSI of 37.8 with a 9.1% weekly loss and -10.1% 4-week relative strength, suggesting a breakdown in progress rather than a buyable dip. I'm neutral on S07 despite its massive 26-week gain because the 4-week relative strength has flatlined near zero and the +39.6% premium to the 200d mean makes it vulnerable to mean reversion.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe at just 0.4% off highs with +31% 12w relative strength; I'd reassess below the 50d mean (~350).
Clean uptrend only 2.5% off highs, RSI 60.7, low volatility (ATR 1.86%), and leading SPY by +6.1% over 4 weeks; would cut below the 50d mean (~281).
Down 23.1% from 52w high, trading 8.7% below 200d mean with negative relative strength—structurally broken; would reconsider only on a sustained move above the 200d.
RSI 37.8 with -9.1% weekly return and -10.1% 4w relative strength signals active distribution, not a dip to buy; need RSI back above 50 and price above the 50d mean to reconsider.
Massive 26w gain of +57.6% but 4w relative strength is flat at +0.1% and price sits 39.6% above the 200d mean—momentum is stalling and mean-reversion risk is high.
Steady but unexciting: RSI 59.6, only 6.6% off highs, but 12w relative strength is -0.4% vs SPY—an in-line performer with no edge either way.
Strong 12w return of +19.4% but sharp 4w pullback of -7.4% and -8.2% relative strength suggest the trend is being tested; wait for stabilization above the 50d mean.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Deliver Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 Faces Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between companies with durable, expanding earnings power and those showing margin erosion. S10 stands out with 85.2% YoY revenue growth, a 71.5% net margin, and net income up 210.6% YoY to $58.3B on minimal debt of $8.5B — this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group by a wide margin. S05 is similarly compelling at 56.9% net margin, 21.8% revenue growth, and 81.2% net income growth on just $14.8B of debt. On the other end, S09 posted a 45.8% YoY decline in net income to $4.2B on a thin 4.9% margin with only 2.4% revenue growth, signaling real earnings deterioration that I cannot look past. S02 is similarly sluggish at 2.0% revenue growth and flat net income, though its 5.6% margin is at least stable. I would need to see margin stabilization or a return to positive earnings growth in S09 and S02 before reconsidering.

views.note: 85% revenue growth, 71.5% net margin, 210% net income growth, and only $8.5B debt — the best earnings profile in the universe.
56.9% net margin with 81% net income growth and low leverage ($14.8B debt) reflects durable, high-quality earnings power.
38.3% net margin, 18.3% revenue growth, and 23.1% net income growth on moderate $40.3B debt is a strong, clean profile.
76.7% net income growth is impressive but 16.7% margin and $122.6B of debt temper my conviction; need to see margin expansion sustain.
Solid 16.6% revenue growth and 26.6% margin, but $82.7B debt load and only 19.4% net income growth keep me neutral pending leverage trajectory.
22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth are encouraging, but 14.6% margin and $36.2B debt on $17.4B revenue is heavy leverage.
33.1% margin is healthy but $448.8B total debt dwarfs revenue; 10% top-line growth and 12.6% earnings growth are adequate but not compelling.
18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are steady but unexciting; $23.9B debt on $21.2B quarterly revenue warrants monitoring.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.2B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin with negligible revenue growth — classic cash-flow compression.
Only 2.0% revenue growth, flat net income, and a 5.6% margin with $77.9B debt suggest limited earnings upside and elevated risk.

memos.headline: Fed Paused but Sticky 3.8% YoY CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensives
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode—the upper bound has held at 3.75% for three months even as the effective rate sits at 3.63%, down 70bp over the past year from prior easing. However, CPI is running at 3.8% YoY with a 1.8% three-month gain (roughly 7.2% annualized), which is far too hot for the Fed to resume cutting anytime soon. The 10y yield has surged 42bp over three months to 4.55%, while the 10y-2y spread has compressed 13bp to +0.42pp, signaling the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and potentially slower growth ahead. Unemployment at 4.3% is stable but has crept up 10bp YoY, consistent with a mild slowdown rather than recession. A downside surprise in the next CPI print (below 3.5% YoY) or a jump in unemployment above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward renewed easing expectations and favor duration-sensitive growth.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face headwinds from the 42bp rise in 10y yields and sticky inflation keeping the Fed on hold.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (10y-2y at +0.42pp) and stable short rates supporting net interest margins in a pause regime.
Staples offer defensive positioning as the macro mix of sticky inflation and rising unemployment hints at late-cycle dynamics.
Energy is a mixed bag—inflation supports pricing power but a mild slowdown could cap demand; I lack conviction either way.
Cyclicals are vulnerable as the yield curve flattening and creeping unemployment signal decelerating growth ahead.
Long-duration growth sectors face the most pain from the 10y yield at 4.55% and no near-term prospect of rate cuts given 3.8% CPI.

memos.headline: Earnings-Season Sentiment Divergence: S05 and S07 Lead Positive Momentum While S04 and S10 Flash Warning Signs
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available. S05 (+10.0%) and S07 (+9.9%) posted the strongest one-day reactions to their Q-results filings on 4/29–4/30, and S05 continues to generate a high volume of 8-K activity including a material definitive agreement filed just yesterday (6/4), suggesting an active narrative that has not yet exhausted itself. S02 (+7.0%) also showed strong positive sentiment on its 4/21 earnings release, though the follow-up filing cadence has been quieter. On the negative side, S04 saw a -3.9% reaction to its 4/29 earnings followed by a management change on 5/14, and S10 posted -1.8% on its 5/20 results with two separate director departure/appointment filings in the preceding weeks—both patterns I associate with deteriorating internal sentiment. I have lower conviction on S06, which has the highest filing volume in the universe (eight 8-Ks since mid-April including bylaws amendments and rights modifications) but only a muted -0.8% earnings reaction; the noise-to-signal ratio there is too high for me to take a directional view.

views.note: Strongest earnings-day pop (+10.0%) in the universe plus sustained high-frequency 8-K activity culminating in a material agreement on 6/4 signals a positive narrative still building.
Near-double-digit +9.9% earnings reaction on 4/30 is a clear positive sentiment inflection, though limited follow-up filings leave me slightly less confident than S05.
Strong +7.0% earnings reaction on 4/21 and a subsequent Reg FD disclosure suggest management is actively engaging investors, but the quieter filing cadence since May tempers conviction.
The -3.9% earnings-day selloff on 4/29 combined with a director/officer change on 5/14 points to negative sentiment momentum that likely has not fully priced.
Two director departure/appointment filings in late April and early May followed by a -1.8% earnings reaction on 5/20 suggest internal instability and negative tone.
Mild -1.0% earnings reaction and a management change shortly after are modestly negative, but the signal is too weak to take a directional stance.

Extremely high filing volume (eight 8-Ks including bylaws and rights modifications) creates noise that overwhelms the muted -0.8% earnings reaction; I cannot separate signal from governance housekeeping.
A +3.2% earnings reaction on 4/30 is constructive, though the preceding officer change filing adds some uncertainty and the filing cadence has been quiet since.
Modest +1.7% Q3 earnings reaction on 4/24 is mildly positive but not strong enough to signal a decisive sentiment shift.
Barely positive +0.8% earnings reaction and routine shareholder-vote filing suggest flat sentiment with no clear catalyst.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Surging Oil Prices Signal Persistent Geopolitical Risk Despite Falling VIX
memos.body: I see a striking divergence between market-implied volatility (VIX at 15.40, down 27% over three months) and the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 363.49, which has surged nearly 58% over the same period. WTI crude at $96.83/bbl is up almost 30% in three months, suggesting energy-security and supply-chain pressures remain acute even as credit spreads tighten modestly (HY OAS at 2.74%). The flattening yield curve (10y-2y at 0.42pp, down 13bp in three months) reinforces my view that markets are pricing in policy-driven growth headwinds. I have higher conviction on names with heavy 8-K disclosure cadence—S05 and S06 each filed multiple times in recent weeks, which I read as active engagement with evolving regulatory or geopolitical developments—and lower conviction where disclosure is sparse. A material escalation in sanctions, export controls, or energy supply disruptions would shift my stance more defensively across the board.

views.note: Three 8-K filings in under a month including a combined 7.01/8.01 on June 4 suggest the company is navigating active policy or regulatory developments; I stay neutral until content clarifies direction.
Five 8-K filings since mid-April is an unusually high cadence, consistent with a company managing geopolitical or regulatory exposure; elevated policy uncertainty keeps me sidelined.
Two Reg FD filings in April but no follow-up since; with policy uncertainty still near 364 and oil near $97, I lack enough company-specific signal to take a directional view.

Two 8-K filings in April suggest some policy-related activity, but the 30% three-month oil surge and elevated uncertainty index argue for caution until we see clearer supply-chain or energy-cost implications.
Single Reg FD filing in April provides minimal geopolitical signal; the 58% three-month jump in policy uncertainty warrants a wait-and-see posture.
Only one Reg FD filing in May amid a macro backdrop of surging oil and elevated policy uncertainty; without evidence of proactive risk management I lean cautious.
